page: Microsoft Azure D248lds_v7 is a high-density, compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv7 server family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 248 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 496.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This low-memory-to-CPU ratio positions the server specifically for compute-heavy operations that do not require massive memory footprints.

The server includes 15118 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not feature any integrated graphics processing units, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or GPU-bound machine learning tasks. The substantial local storage capacity allows for high-throughput local data operations directly on the host.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D248lds_v7 offers a specialized hardware profile that minimizes memory overhead to maximize raw CPU allocation. This resource density is advantageous for workloads where licensing or infrastructure costs are tied to compute capacity rather than memory size. Recommended workloads include high-performance computing, large-scale batch processing, compute-intensive simulations, and distributed data processing tasks that can leverage the massive 248-vCPU parallelization alongside its extensive local storage.
